thread.title: How hard is it to be a stock-market bear right now? This chart drives it home - MarketWatch

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: How hard is it to be a stock-market bear right now? This chart drives it home - MarketWatch
text:
It’s back to the drawing board for investors, after the State of the Union delivered no big bells or whistles for Wall Street.
There’s some lingering disappointment in the air, with stocks looking at a down day, possibly due to the fact POTUS didn’t lay down big news on a trade deal with China, outside of some promises for progress. For better or worse, the commander-in-chief also didn’t make a single mention of the shutdown.
He did say we have the “hottest economy in the world.” OK, perhaps minus Poland and Latvia, but we’re almost No. 1!
#Trump claimed the US economy is "considered far and away the hottest economy anywhere in the world.” In fact, the economies of Latvia, Poland, China, India and Greece are growing much faster. https://t.co/ffjoyAWSls
— Neil Marshall #FBPE (@ANMarshall) February 6, 2019 But no news is good news? “There was no escalation of tensions – at least not meaningfully. There was no talk of using Commander in Chief military powers to build the wall, for instance. That might be considered a win for investors, who prefer it when things do not escalate,” Paul Donovan, global chief economist at UBS, told clients this morning.
Clearly though, investors are looking for reasons to keep what has been an impressive rally since the start of the year going. And they may need to look harder now that earnings season is winding down. Saying that, our chart of the day , from Slope of Hope’s Tim Knight shows why it’s so hard for stock investors to remain in the bear camp these days.
It’s a multiyear chart of the AdvisorShares Ranger Equity Bear ETF HDGE, -0.27% or HDGE, an ETF that caters to the bears, by offering a strategy that involves selling stocks short. Knight notes it is just about to hit an all-time low:
“It seems to me this one simple chart illustrates swiftly and painfully just how the bearish world has fallen to pieces since Christmas and [Treasury Secretary Steven] Mnuchin’s phone call from Cabo. HDGE has fallen virtually every single day, much as it had risen almost every single day from Dec. 3 (the G-20 trade truce) until Dec. 26,” says Knight, on his blog .
“No doubt about it. For 2019 so far, it absolutely sucks to be bearish,” he adds.
Since we’re talking charts, last word goes to Naeem Aslam, chief market analyst at ThinkMarkets U.K., who may have some good news for those cowering bears. His own chart shows below-average volumes for one widely held S&P 500 ETF SPY, -0.14% :
Naeem Aslam, Think Makets U.K. “The S&P 500 is up 9.21% year-to-date, the NASDAQ index is up 11.51% year to date and the Dow Jones is up 8.93% YTD. There are some genuine concerns that the markets are moving higher without any strong volume behind them and a trend like this doesn’t end well,” said Aslam.
The market The Dow DJIA, -0.09% S&P 500 SPX, -0.22% and Nasdaq COMP, -0.37% are off to a slow start. Read more in Market Snapshot
The dollar DXY, +0.30% is up, largely due to a biggish drop in the Aussie dollar AUDUSD, -1.6310% after the central bank there stopped short of an expected dovish shift. Crude US:CLU8 is slightly lower and gold GCJ9, -0.62% is also softer.
Europe stocks SXXP, +0.15% are struggling, and in Asia, where most markets remain on vacation, the Nikkei NIK, +0.14% and Aussie stocks XJO, +0.34% both closed up slightly .
The call Snapchat parent Snap SNAP, +22.59% is up in a big way after posting a narrower-than-expected loss, but our call of the day from analysts at Sig Susquehanna, says don’t fall for that “not-as-bad-as-expected rally.” Analysts Shyam Patil and Brendan McGoldrick say take advantage of any gains, as they sit on a negative rating and $5 price target.
“We see competition from Facebook/Instagram (IG Stories 500 million + daily active users vs. SNAP’s 186 million), a saturated core demo (and a weak presence outside the U.S.), issues with Android, and lackluster ad products (with subpar return on investments) as continuing to pose challenges for the company…and we don’t think the CFO would’ve left after only eight months if the business was about to turn,” said the analysts.
Shares are still trading at a premium to Facebook FB, -0.36% and Twitter TWTR, -0.39% when it comes to one valuation measure — enterprise value to sales, Sig Susquehanna analysts add. Read more from own Therese Poletti, who lays out just how much Snapchat parent still has to prove.
The buzz It isn’t moving stocks, but POTUS’s State of the Union address will drive some chatter Wednesday. There has been a fairly mixed reaction by lawmakers, after he urged them to reject “the policy of revenge,” and didn’t offer much in return for building his wall. As expected, he announced a second summit with North Korea’s Kim Jong Un in Vietnam this month, but eyebrows are up after he took credit for “preventing a major war” with that country:
“If I had not been elected President of the US, we would right now, in my opinion, be in a major war with North Korea with potentially millions of people killed.” - Trump
Fact check: Are you kidding me?
— ian bremmer (@ianbremmer) February 6, 2019 Georgia Dem. Stacey Abrams: I don’t want Trump to fail, but ‘we need him to tell the truth’
After a big entrance six years ago to transform Apple AAPL, -0.04% into a more luxury brand, retail chief Angela Ahrendts is leaving . Analysts at Wedbush aren’t too worried, especially given company veteran Deirdre O’Brien is taking over her spot:
“We are encouraged that a core Apple insider took over the reins at this juncture as an outsider running retail going into one of the most pivotal, defining periods for Cook & Co. in the company’s history would have been a risky endeavor,” said Daniel Ives and his colleagues in a note.
Tesla TSLA, -1.07% shares are up, and here’s CEO Elon Musk talking Model 3 prices.
Model 3 starting cost now ~$35k (after ~$8k of credits & fuel savings) https://t.co/46TXqRrsdr
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) February 6, 2019 The Oscars will be host-less for the first time in 30 years, as the Academy has had a tough time filling the big job after comedian Kevin Hart pulled out in December.
Earnings GM GM, +1.93% is climbing after topping earnings estimates. Results are also through for Eil Lilly LLY, -0.81% Boston Scientific BSX, +2.79% Humana HUM, -0.67% HUM, -0.67% HUM, -0.67% Spotify SPOT, -2.76% and Goodyear GT, -0.38%
After the close, we’ll get Zynga ZNGA, -1.64% MetLife MET, +0.13% Take-Two TTWO, -13.65% FireEye FEYE, -0.46% Match MTCH, -4.54% and Equifax EFX, -0.71%
Electronic Arts EA, -13.27% is facing its worst-decline since 1999 after the videogame maker fell short of holiday-season sales estimates and cut its forecast. There was better news from Disney DIS, -1.15% and shares are up a little.
The economy The U.S. trade deficit dipped in November, according to some shutdown delayed catch-up data , while a not-complete look at fourth-quarter productivity showed a gain of 1.3% . Later, we’ll hear from Fed Chairman Jerome Powell, who is due to give brief opening remarks at a teacher town hall at 7 p.m. Eastern.
The stat $250,000 — That’s the monthly cost of being Cardi B, who told fans in a Twitter video Tuesday that neither her lifestyle nor taking care of her entire family comes cheap. And she says as the IRS takes a 45% chunk of her earnings, she has to make “at least a million” to spend half that. Here’s what FinTwit thinks she can do better:
